title: H169 — LLM-augmented 10-K embedding pair selection for H160
rationale: arXiv:2604.19476 (Huang, Fan, Hu, Ye — April 2026) demonstrates a two-stage pairs trading framework: (1) build a sparse candidate graph from 10-K text embeddings (companies with similar business descriptions are likely to share risk factors), (2) use an LLM to classify and filter candidate edges by economic relation quality. Tested on S&P 500 2011-2019: long-short Sharpe improved from 0.742 to 0.820, MaxDD reduced from -10.47% to -7.85%. This directly improves H160 (factor-residualized equity pairs) by replacing ad-hoc pair selection (MSFT/TXN, TXN/META, etc.) with a principled LLM-filtered semantic network approach. The embedding step requires 10-K text (available via edgartools), and the LLM filter can run with Claude/GPT-4o on a per-pair basis. PREREQUISITE: H160 must confirm factor residualization first — this is a H160+ upgrade, not a standalone.
content: h169_status: QUEUED (dream cycle 2026-05-04) — LLM-Augmented Pair Selection for H160+: use 10-K text embeddings + LLM edge filtering to improve equity pair selection beyond ad-hoc choices. arXiv:2604.19476 (April 2026): sparse candidate graph from sentence-BERT 10-K embeddings → LLM classifies economic relations → cointegration-filtered pairs. S&P 500 2011-2019: Sharpe 0.742→0.820, MaxDD -10.47%→-7.85%. Method: (1) download 10-K Item 1 (business description) for target universe via edgartools, (2) compute sentence-BERT embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 22M params, fast), (3) build candidate pairs graph (cosine sim > 0.7), (4) LLM filter: for each candidate pair, ask 'Does company A and company B share common risk factors that would cause cointegration?' (yes/no + reasoning), (5) run cointegration test on LLM-approved pairs only. Libraries: sentence-transformers (pip install sentence-transformers), edgartools. Data: 10-K annual filings via EDGAR. PREREQUISITE: H160 (factor-residualized pairs) must reach PARTIAL or CONFIRMED first. Estimated 15h. Queue after H160.
